record.paper_title: Analysis on Faddeev Knots and Skyrme Solitons: Recent Progress and Open Problems
record.original_question: Let X = {n : R^3 → S^2, E(n) < ∞} be the finite-energy Sobolev class for the Faddeev model. Does every map n in X admit approximation by smooth maps n_j ∈ C∞(R^3, S^2) with uniformly bounded energy such that n_j → n in H^1_loc(R^3, S^2)?

evidence.quote: is well defined. Moreover, Q(n) ∈ Z as was shown in Theorem 3.3 of [50]. It is not clear, however, if any map n ∈ X can be approximated in L2_loc by a sequence of smooth maps nj ∈ C∞(R3, S2) such that E(nj) remains uniformly bounded. It is certainly unknown if n ∈ X can be approximated by a sequence of nj ∈ C∞(R3, S2) such that nj → n in H1_loc(R3, S2) and E(nj) remains to be uniformly bounded, as j → ∞. We refer to [37, 38, 39] for some recent works concerning such density questions of smooth maps in the spaces of Sobolev maps.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a measurable map $n:\mathbb{R}^3\to S^2$ (where $S^2$ denotes the unit sphere in $\mathbb{R}^3$), define the Faddeev energy
$$E(n)=\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}\bigl(|\nabla n|^2+|n^{*}\omega|^2\bigr)\,dx,$$
where $n^{*}\omega$ is the pullback by $n$ of the standard area form $\omega$ on $S^2$, i.e., $(n^{*}\omega)_{ij}=n\cdot(\partial_i n\wedge\partial_j n)$, and $|n^{*}\omega|^2=\sum_{i<j}|(n^{*}\omega)_{ij}|^2$. Let
$$X=\{\,n:\mathbb{R}^3\to S^2 \ \text{measurable} : E(n)<\infty\,\}.$$
Question: Does every $n\in X$ admit a sequence of smooth maps $n_j\in C^\infty(\mathbb{R}^3,S^2)$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\sup_{j} E(n_j)<\infty$, and
\item $n_j\to n$ in $H^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb{R}^3,S^2)$ as $j\to\infty$?
\end{enumerate}
Equivalently, are smooth $S^2$-valued maps with uniformly bounded Faddeev energy $H^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$-dense in the finite-energy class $X$?
artifact.category_tag: Density of smooth maps in Sobolev spaces (Faddeev model)
artifact.status_search_result: The question of $H^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$-density of smooth maps with uniformly bounded Faddeev energy in the finite-energy class is highlighted as unresolved in the surveyed literature on the Faddeev model. Related works (e.g., Hang–Lin on $S^2$-valued maps and Faddeev's model, and Giaquinta–Mucci-type relaxed-energy approximations) establish density only for weaker topologies or for maps smooth away from finitely many points; no full $H^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$ smooth approximation result with energy bound has been reported.

status_evidence.title: Analysis of S^2-Valued Maps and Faddeev's Model
status_evidence.snippet: Homotopy/topological invariants extend to finite Faddeev energy maps; density of smooth maps studied in weak topology.
status_evidence.claim: Strong smooth-map density in finite-Faddeev-energy class is not established.

status_evidence.title: A new approximation of relaxed energies for harmonic maps and the Faddeev model
status_evidence.snippet: Approximation method for relaxed Faddeev energy; minimizers exist for Hopf degree ±1.
status_evidence.claim: Only relaxed/weak approximation results are available; the H^1_loc smooth approximation question remains addressed only partially.

status_evidence.title: The Pontrjagin-Hopf invariants for Sobolev maps
status_evidence.snippet: Best one can hope is density of maps smooth except at finitely many points.
status_evidence.claim: Full smooth density may fail; topological obstructions are known.
